arxiv-1609-03825.title: Measurement of the photon and jet production with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-1609-03825.creator: Michal Svatoš, On behalf of the ATLAS Collaboration, [1ex] Institute of Physics, AV CR, Na Slovance 1999/2, Prague, Czech Republic
arxiv-1609-03825.description: Abstract Production of prompt isolated photons at hadron colliders provides a probe of perturbative QCD and can be used to study the gluon density function of the proton. The ATLAS collaboration has performed precise measurements of the inclusive production of isolated prompt photons in 20.2 fb -1 of data collected at s = 8 \sqrt{s}=8 TeV and in 6.

arxiv-2211-02510.title: GOODS-ALMA 2.0: Last gigayear star formation histories of the so-called starbursts within the main sequence
arxiv-2211-02510.creator: L. Ciesla, C. Gómez-Guijarro, V. Buat, D. Elbaz, S. Jin, M. Béthermin, E. Daddi, M. Franco, H. Inami, G. Magdis, and B. Magnelli
arxiv-2211-02510.description: Abstract Recently, a population of compact main sequence (MS) galaxies exhibiting starburst-like properties have been identified in the GOODS-ALMA blind survey at 1.1 mm. Several evolution scenarios were proposed to explain their particular physical properties (e.g., compact size, low gas content, short depletion time).

arxiv-2303-04512.title: Theory of Josephson current on a lattice model of grain boundary in d d -wave superconductors Journal: Supercond. Sci. Technol.
arxiv-2303-04512.creator: Takashi Sakamori, Satoshi Kashiwaya, Rikizo Yano, Yukio Tanaka, Takafumi Hatano, Keiji Yada
arxiv-2303-04512.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Takashi Sakamori, Satoshi Kashiwaya, Rikizo Yano, Yukio Tanaka, Takafumi Hatano, Keiji Yada. Identifying the origins of suppression of the critical current at grain boundaries of high-critical-temperature superconductors, such as cuprates and iron-based superconductors, is a crucial issue to be solved for future applications with polycrystalline materials. Although the dominant factor of current suppression might arise during material fabrication and/or processing, investigating it due to an internal phase change of the pair potential is an important issue in understanding the threshold of the critical current.

arxiv-2401-01899.title: Free space optical link to a tethered balloon for frequency transfer and chronometric geodesy Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2401-01899.creator: Nicolas Maron, 1,2 Sébastien Fernandez, 1,2 François-Xavier Esnault, 2 Thomas Lévèque, 2 Tepuaonini Muzeau 3 and Peter Wolf 1,*
arxiv-2401-01899.description: Abstract We present the results of an optical link to a corner cube on board a tethered balloon at 300 m altitude including a Tip/Tilt compensation for the balloon tracking. Our experiment measures the carrier phase of a 1542 nm laser, which is the useful signal for frequency comparison of distant clocks.

arxiv-2404-05858.title: A Neuromorphic Approach to Obstacle Avoidance in Robot Manipulation
arxiv-2404-05858.creator: Ahmed Faisal Abdelrahman \affilnum 1, Matias Valdenegro-Toro \affilnum 2, Maren Bennewitz \affilnum 3 and Paul G. Plöger \affilnum 1
arxiv-2404-05858.description: Abstract Neuromorphic computing mimics computational principles of the brain in silico and motivates research into event-based vision and spiking neural networks (SNNs). Event cameras (ECs) exclusively capture local intensity changes and offer superior power consumption, response latencies, and dynamic ranges.

arxiv-2411-04172.title: Light-cone actions and correlators of self-dual theories in AdS 4
arxiv-2411-04172.creator: Chandramouli Chowdhury, George Doran, Arthur Lipstein, Ricardo Monteiro, Silvia Nagy, and Kajal Singh
arxiv-2411-04172.description: Abstract Self-dual Yang-Mills and Einstein gravity in Euclidean AdS 4 are useful toy models because they can be described by simple scalar Lagrangians exhibiting a new manifestation of the colour/kinematics duality, as recently shown by two of the authors. In this paper, we clarify how the self-dual sectors fit into the full theories.

arxiv-2506-20269.title: Narrative Shift Detection: A Hybrid Approach of Dynamic Topic Models and Large Language Models
arxiv-2506-20269.creator: Kai-Robin Lange, Tobias Schmidt, Matthias Reccius, Henrik Müller, Michael Roos, Carsten Jentsch
arxiv-2506-20269.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kai-Robin Lange, Tobias Schmidt, Matthias Reccius, Henrik Müller, Michael Roos, Carsten Jentsch. With rapidly evolving media narratives, it has become increasingly critical to not just extract narratives from a given corpus but rather investigate, how they develop over time. While popular narrative extraction methods such as Large Language Models do well in capturing typical narrative elements or even the complex structure of a narrative, applying them to an entire corpus comes with obstacles, such as a high financial or computational cost.

arxiv-2510-11332.title: Operator Ranges and Spaceability: Extending a Result of Kitson and Timoney
arxiv-2510-11332.creator: Geivison Ribeiro
arxiv-2510-11332.description: Abstract . We revisit the results of Kitson and Timoney [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 378 (2011), 680–686] on the spaceability of complements of operator ranges, extending one of their main theorems to the general Fréchet setting. In particular, we provide an affirmative answer to the question posed in Remark 3.

arxiv-2512-04523.title: An accelerated proximal bundle method for convex optimization
arxiv-2512-04523.creator: Feng-Yi Liao, Thomas Madden, Yang Zheng
arxiv-2512-04523.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Feng-Yi Liao, Thomas Madden, Yang Zheng. The proximal bundle method (PBM) is a powerful and widely used approach for minimizing nonsmooth convex functions. However, for smooth objectives, its best-known convergence rate remains suboptimal, and whether PBM can be accelerated remains open. In this work, we present the first accelerated proximal bundle method that achieves the optimal 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 / ϵ ) \mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{\epsilon}) iteration complexity for obtaining an ϵ \epsilon -accurate solution in smooth convex optimization.

pmc-11599295.title: Thoracolumbar injuries: non operative treatment: indications, management
pmc-11599295.creator: Christoph Nau, Hans Christoph Pape, Marko Jug, Klaus Wendt, Radko Komadina, Frank Bloemers
pmc-11599295.description: IntroductionThoracolumbar spine injuries can result from various traumatic events such as falls, motor vehicle accidents, and sports injuries. While surgical intervention is often indicated for complex fractures and in case of neurological deficits, non-operative treatment remains a viable option for certain types of injuries.

pmc-11714489.title: Feasibility of Telehealth Memory Assessments for a Mild Cognitive Impairment Registry: Lessons Learned from a Clinical Coordinator
pmc-11714489.creator: Faith Stagge, Alyssa M Lanzi, Matthew L. Cohen, Curtis L Johnson, Christopher R. Martens
pmc-11714489.description: BackgroundTo create de novo infrastructure for ADRD research, The Delaware (DE) Center for Cognitive Aging Research (DECCAR) began a telehealth‐based mild cognitive impairment (MCI) registry. The registry included a dynamic recruitment plan and remote intake procedures to classify community‐dwelling adults as having MCI from probable Alzheimer’s Disease.

pmc-12428462.title: Should I Stay at Home Alone? Lived Experiences of Loneliness Among Older Adults: A Qualitative Study
pmc-12428462.creator: Maria Shuk Yu Hung, Michael Man Ho Li, Ken Hok Man Ho, Victor Manuel Mendoza-Nuñez
pmc-12428462.description: Background: Loneliness and social isolation among older people are currently widespread and recognized as the foremost public health problems globally and locally. Hong Kong, which exhibits a rapid aging trend and an expanding elderly population, is inevitably facing these issues. This study explored the lived experiences of loneliness among older adults in Hong Kong.

pmc-12513139.title: A genome-wide investigation of insidious uveitis in Appaloosa horses
pmc-12513139.creator: N B Kingsley, L Sandmeyer, A Dwyer, C D Langefeld, R J McMullen, M McCue, M Lassaline, R R Bellone
pmc-12513139.description: BackgroundEquine recurrent uveitis (ERU), an inflammatory eye disease, is the leading cause of blindness among horses. pmc-12547578.title: Mechanisms of Barium Sulfate Dissolution through the Lens of Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
pmc-12547578.creator: Nikolai Trofimov, Andreas Luttge, Inna Kurganskaya
pmc-12547578.description: The prediction of crystalline matter dissolution kinetics is one of the main focuses in environmental science, civil engineering, chemical kinetics, synthesis, drug delivery, and other scientific and industrial fields. Our ability to predict the temporal dynamics of material fluxes is crucial for designing crystalline materials and controlling the behavior of chemical systems for various applications.

pmc-12635660.title: Application of electromyographic biofeedback therapy in physical dysfunction rehabilitation and post-stroke anxiety reduction in stroke survivors
pmc-12635660.creator: Li Yu, Hao Niu, Wen-Bin Ji, Zhi-Gang Liu, Bin Jiang, Wei-Ya Wang
pmc-12635660.description: BACKGROUNDStroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide, and limb motor dysfunction is one of the most common complications affecting the quality of life of patients.AIMTo investigate the rehabilitation effects of conventional rehabilitation training combined with electromyographic biofeedback therapy on limb motor dysfunction in stroke survivors.

pmc-12690812.title: Real-world prescriptions of GLP-1RAs and SGLT2is in type 2 diabetes prioritise BMI and age over cardiorenal risk: a machine learning-based large cohort analysis
pmc-12690812.creator: Dario Tuccinardi, Rita Zilich, Paola Ponzani, Nicoletta Musacchio, Valeria Manicardi, Alberto Rocca, Roberto Pontremoli, Paola Fioretto, Andrea Muscarà, Graziano Di Cianni, Riccardo Candido, Salvatore A De Cosmo, Giuseppina Russo
pmc-12690812.description: BackgroundUnderstanding how SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) and GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are prescribed in relation to cardiorenal risk is crucial for assessing adherence to guidelines and optimize outcomes in type 2 diabetes (T2D). This study aimed to determine whether prescription patterns across different cardiorenal phenotypic subgroups reflect clinical risk or are affected by demographic factors.

pmc-12769749.title: Syndemic perspective of how people living with HIV faced the COVID-19 crisis in North Africa
pmc-12769749.creator: Marion Di Ciaccio, Othmane Bourhaba, Elisa Adami, Nassima Boulahdour, Amal Ben Moussa, Mustapha Sodqi, Souhaila Bensaid, Lucas Riegel, Daniela Rojas Castro, Mehdi Karkouri, Nicolas Lorente
pmc-12769749.description: The 2020–2023 COVID-19 pandemic impacted societies and healthcare access worldwide, including HIV services. Changes in access exacerbated social inequalities in health among socially underserved groups including people living with HIV (PLHIV). This study aimed to explore PLHIV’s psychosocial experience of the COVID-19 pandemic in the MENA region using a syndemic approach.
